chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Haytham al-Nahdi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali (peace be upon him): In

a man gave a man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a solitary Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad). He said: 'He is not permitted to perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) with the Umrah to the Hajj, so as not to contradict the owner of the dirhams.' The first point in it is that it is a suspended hadith (mawquf), not fully connected to one of the Imams (peace be upon them). And this ruling is not abandoned because of it, the connected reports. The first hadith is connected, so taking it is preferable. And if it were safe from that, it would be interpreted as referring to one who gave another a Hajj from the residents of Mecca and the Sanctuary, because one whose ruling is this is not upon him the Tamattu', so it is not permissible for one who performs Hajj on his behalf to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah to the Hajj. And the first hadith would be inclusive of one upon whom Tamattu' with the Umrah to the Hajj is obligatory, so he performs Hajj on his behalf likewise, then it suffices for him even if he had been ordered with the Solitary Hajj. And one who deposited money with another then died, there is no harm that the depositor performs Hajj on his behalf and returns what remained of that to his heirs. Narrated.

key_terms.بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: With the Umrah to the Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an agent performing Hajj on behalf of someone who paid for a solitary Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent conflict between a mawqūf report and a musnad narration by prioritizing the authenticated chain, while offering a contextual interpretation that the restriction on Tamattu' applies specifically to agents of Mecca residents. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of fidelity to the principal's (muwakkil) specific intent in delegated worship, ensuring the agent's ritual form aligns with the payer's designated Hajj type. The text further clarifies the financial mechanics of Hajj al-Nafi, affirming that surplus funds from the delegated pilgrimage revert to the payer's heirs upon death.
